_note: Round 4 profiles, written before any round-4 observation on either engine (app/scoring_v2.php; Open edX ORA2 at commit 96b4ad10). New profiles are listed under 'profiles'; the 16 profiles of rounds 1-3 are reused for ORA2 with the metadata in 'prior_profiles_meta'. Format as in rounds 1-3, plus: 'aggregate' (how the framework's documents combine ratings into an overall score: weighted_sum, mean_within_element, min, none_defined, uncertain), 'na_allowed' (an element may be marked not applicable and leave the denominator), 'uncertain' (properties not verifiable from the cited source; a profile with any prediction-relevant uncertain property is excluded from the primary analysis of that engine, never guessed). A scale written as {"continuous": [lo, hi]} means any real value in [lo, hi].

sources.CAF2020FT: CAF 2020, EIPA, https://www.eipa.eu/wp-content/uploads/2023/02/CAF_2020_English.pdf, ch. III 'How to evaluate: the scoring system', pp. 53-56: a score per subcriterion from 0 to 100 on six levels; fine-tuned enablers panel gives a score per PLAN/DO/CHECK/ACT phase and 'Calculate a global score by considering the average of the scores of each phase' (p. 55); fine-tuned results panel gives a trend score and a target score, global = their average (p. 56); no rule combining subcriterion scores into a criterion or overall total is given (pp. 53-56).
sources.BaldrigeHC2023: 2023-2024 Baldrige Excellence Framework (Health Care), free sample, NIST, https://www.nist.gov/document/2023-2024-baldrige-framework-hc-free-samplepdf, pp. i-ii (seven categories; category 7 Results with items 7.1-7.5; 'Performance against Health Care Criteria items is scored on two evaluation dimensions: process and results', p. 30 per contents; process scoring guidelines p. 32, results p. 33, point values p. 35) and p. 15 (item 3.2 marked PROCESS). Pages 30-35 are not in the free sample.
sources.EdPEx_aggregate: app/scoring.php line 13 (roll-up: item = % x points, category sum, overall sum, max 1000); config/edpex.json _meta.source_points_table (EdPEx 2567-2570, items and point values, p. 21).
sources.W_variants: Synthetic; generated by the rule in SPEC.md, section 'Variant rule', written before predict_round4.py was run.

excluded_unverifiable.ABEF: Australian Business Excellence Framework: public sources found (e.g. City of Joondalup policy, https://www.joondalup.wa.gov.au/wp-content/uploads/2023/05/Australian-Business-Excellence-Framework-CP-1.pdf) state seven categories and ADRI, but no accessible official document gives the rating scale, levels or aggregation.
excluded_unverifiable.SBE: Singapore Business Excellence framework: Enterprise Singapore (https://enterprisesg.gov.sg/grow-your-business/boost-capabilities/quality-and-standards/business-excellence) states the recognition programme closed in 2020; no official scoring document was accessible.
excluded_unverifiable.JQA: Japan Quality Award: only secondary descriptions found (1,000 points; levels D to AAA+, 11 steps); the official assessment criteria book (Japan Productivity Center) was not accessible, so values per level and the aggregation cannot be cited.
excluded_unverifiable.ISO9004_2018: ISO 9004:2018 Annex A (self-assessment, maturity levels): the standard is paywalled (iso.org OBP returned HTTP 403); secondary sources do not reproduce the level values or any aggregation rule.
excluded_unverifiable.BaldrigeHC2023_scale: Included as a profile, but its scale, factor levels, point values and aggregation are on pp. 30-35, which are not in the free sample; marked uncertain.
